question.text: Will a second televised debate between Taipei mayoral candidates Chiang Wan-an and Puma Shen be scheduled by November 13, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, by 23:59 Taipei time (UTC+8) on November 13, 2026, a specific calendar date has been publicly announced for a second televised debate between Taipei mayoral candidates Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) and Puma Shen (沈伯洋), as reported on [CNA's 2026 election topic page](https://www.cna.com.tw/topic/newstopic/5100.aspx) or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). "Second televised debate" means any debate other than the October 31, 2026 TVBS/SET event: an event produced by a media outlet and broadcast on a television channel or that outlet's live online stream, in which both candidates appear together in a debate format — taking questions from each other and/or from journalists, as in the October 31 event — rather than separate solo appearances such as a 政見發表會 (policy presentation). A date counts as announced only if it is reported as agreed by both campaigns, or as confirmed by the hosting outlet(s)/organizer with both candidates participating; a date proposed or accepted by only one campaign does not count, and an announced date still counts even if the debate is later postponed or cancelled. If no such date has been announced by the deadline, this question resolves NO.
question.fine_print: Any host qualifies — a single broadcaster, a consortium of media outlets, or another organizer — provided both campaigns are confirmed participants. If several additional debates are announced by the deadline, the announcement of any one of them suffices.

research:
I could not find any report, as of 2026-11-03, that a date has been set for a second Chiang-Shen debate. Both campaigns now say they are open to one, and their campaign managers have made contact. But the media group invited the candidates on October 31, and I found no sign yet that it has called the meeting to negotiate terms.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: CNA's 2026 election topic page lists these debate items, all without a date for a second debate:
  - Nov 3, 13:02: "蔣萬安：傾向參加第2次辯論會　談定形式、時間就願意" (Chiang leans toward a second debate and is willing once format and time are agreed)
  - Nov 2, 19:02: Shen says Chiang did not answer the debate questions and used them to attack instead
  - Nov 2, 11:51: "第2場辯論？蔣萬安：由團隊協調" (Chiang says his team will coordinate)
  - Nov 2, 11:07: Taichung Mayor Lu Shiow-yen on the controversy over questions shared in advance
  [CNA](https://www.cna.com.tw/topic/newstopic/5100.aspx)

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. Neither campaign nor any media outlet has announced or confirmed a date. A news roundup also says the date and format of a second debate were still open as of Nov 2. [GVM](https://city.gvm.com.tw/article/133644)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: On Shen Chun-hua's online show (recorded Nov 2), Chiang said "我傾向於參加" (I lean toward taking part) and that he has "of course" got confidence. He said his team would set the time, details and format with the other side. He noted that the first debate took two rounds of negotiation and that the other camp "has different ideas." [UDN](https://udn.com/news/story/124652/9853637), [Next Apple](https://news.nextapple.com/politics/20261103/45E6ECCC964D2A9114D8B9342250C511), [Mirror Media](https://www.mirrormedia.mg/story/20261103edi025)
- 2026-11-03: China Times reports that the second debate is still unconfirmed and that Chiang has passed the matter to his team. I could not open the page (HTTP 403), so this comes from the news API summary. [China Times](https://ivoting.chinatimes.com/20261103001917-261001)
- 2026-11-02:
  - Shen's campaign manager Wu Sz-yao (吳思瑤) added Chiang's campaign manager Lo Chih-chiang (羅智強) on LINE to discuss the next debate.
  - Lo said Chiang's side "has always been open" and is waiting for the Liberty Times-led media group to send a negotiation invitation.
  - Lo also mocked Shen, listing "rules" Shen's side should prepare.
  - Wu expressed regret that no second debate has been confirmed.
  [SETN](https://www.setn.com/news/1932193), [ETtoday](https://www.ettoday.net/news/20261102/3264876.htm), [NOWnews](https://www.nownews.com/news/6883792), [TVBS](https://news.tvbs.com.tw/politics/4044736)
- 2026-11-02:
  - Shen proposed a second debate in which media questions are answered on the spot, without being shared in advance.
  - Chiang said Shen "did not make good use" of the first debate and that his team would coordinate.
  [LTN](https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/politics/breakingnews/5626460), [UDN](https://udn.com/news/story/124652/9853104)
- 2026-11-02: A dispute broke out over debate questions shared before the event. TVBS says both camps agreed to this beforehand, and Lo claims Wu was the first to support it. This friction could make the next negotiation harder. [LTN](https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/Taipei/breakingnews/5626600), [Taiwan News](https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/zh/news/6470098)
- 2026-10-31: Ten outlets issued a joint statement inviting a second debate hosted jointly by several media. The outlets named include Liberty Times, CTV, TTV, FTV, Mirror TV, CTS, ETtoday, EBC and Era. The statement asked the campaigns to "quickly appoint representatives" to negotiate time, venue, rules and broadcast. It gave no date. [China Times](https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20261031003050-260407)
- 2026-10-31: At the end of the first debate, Shen invited Chiang to a second one on stage. Chiang did not accept then. [UDN](https://udn.com/vote2026/story/124652/9853637)

## 4. Base rates
- The first debate in this race took two negotiation rounds over 4 days (Oct 11 invitation, Oct 12 talks, Oct 15 date fixed). [FTV](https://www.ftvnews.com.tw/news/detail/2026A15W0562) If the media group calls talks soon, a date could be fixed within a week.
- From memory, not verified this session: the 2018 and 2022 Taipei mayoral races each had a single televised debate, even though challengers pushed for more. The 2014 race (Ko Wen-je vs Sean Lien) had several.
- Calendar constraints: official campaigning and CEC-run policy presentations run Nov 13-27, and the polling blackout starts Nov 18. Any second debate would have to fit around these, roughly in the window Nov 8-25.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or forecast on whether a second debate will happen.
- Related Kalshi market (fetched 2026-11-03), Taipei mayor winner: Chiang 0.60, Shen 0.38. Polymarket "KMT sweep" (Taipei and New Taipei): 0.41.
- Context, polls:
  - TVBS post-debate poll: 47% thought Shen performed better vs 40% for Chiang. Overall support still favored Chiang, at 46%. [Storm](https://www.storm.mg/article/11177643)
  - A DPP-leaning AI phone poll had Shen at 52.6% vs Chiang at 35.3%. [SETN](https://www.setn.com/news/1932066)
  - As the frontrunner, Chiang has less incentive to agree to a second debate quickly.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Whether the media group (Liberty Times and partners) sends a formal invitation and convenes talks. Lo says this is what Chiang's side is waiting for. This is the key trigger to watch.
- Negotiations on format may stall. Shen wants questions answered on the spot without advance sharing, while Chiang wants to follow the first debate's format.
- Nov 12: CEC publishes the official candidate list. Nov 13: official campaign period and CEC policy presentations begin. Chiang has previously cited lack of time on his schedule.
- Nov 18: polling blackout begins. A debate after that would come late in the race, which could push the campaigns either to fix a date quickly or to let it lapse.

## 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic data. As I recall (not verified this session), recent Taipei mayoral races (2018, 2022) each had only one televised debate. That fits Chiang's earlier statement that the custom is one TV debate plus the government-run policy presentations.
- In this race, getting the first debate scheduled took about 4 days and 2 negotiation rounds, from the October 11 announcement to the October 15 agreement. Even starting talks now, a comparable pace could produce a date before November 13, but no negotiation meeting has been reported.
- Timing is tight. The official campaign period starts November 13, the polling blackout starts November 18, and election day is November 28. A debate held after about November 22 would leave little time before the vote.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on whether a second debate will happen.
- Related markets (fetched 2026-11-03):

- These don't measure the debate question. They do show Chiang as the front-runner, who usually has less reason to agree to another debate.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Any negotiation meeting called by the ten-outlet media group, or contact between Lo Chih-chiang's and Wu Szu-yao's teams. The main obstacles are format disputes: Shen wants immediate Q&A, and both sides are arguing about scripted answers and leaked questions.
- 2026-11-12: the Central Election Commission (CEC) publishes the official candidate list.
- 2026-11-13: the deadline, which is also the day the campaign period and the CEC-run policy presentations begin.
- 2026-11-18: polling blackout begins. New polls showing Shen gaining could raise pressure on Chiang to agree.
- If an announcement comes, it is most likely to appear on CNA's topic page and in LTN and UDN coverage.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain, until 23:59 Taipei time on November 13, 2026. For Yes, a specific date for a second Chiang-Shen debate (not the October 31 TVBS/SET event) must be publicly reported. It must be either agreed by both campaigns or confirmed by the host outlet(s) with both candidates participating.

(b) The status quo is No. As of November 3, no negotiation meeting has been convened and no date exists.

(c) Base rate: Taipei mayoral races in 2018 and 2022 each had only one televised debate, despite challengers pushing for more. The 2014 race had several. For a frontrunner incumbent who initially resisted a second debate, the base rate of agreeing to one is roughly 25-35%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - On November 3, Chiang said he "leans toward participating" and would do so once format and time are agreed.
  - On November 2, Lo said his side is "open" and waiting for the Liberty Times-led group to convene talks.
  - On October 31, ten outlets issued a joint invitation.
  - The campaign managers made contact on November 2.
  - The first debate took only 4 days from invitation to a fixed date.
- **For No:**
  - Chiang leads (Kalshi 0.60), and the TVBS post-debate poll found 47% thought Shen performed better, so Chiang has little incentive to debate again.
  - Disputes over the format and the questions shared in advance are already surfacing.
  - Lo's mocking tone and his remark that the other camp "has different ideas" point to slow-walking.
  - Chiang has cited lack of time, and from November 13 the official campaign and CEC presentations crowd the calendar.
  - The October 12 "no time" stance shows his reluctance.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The media group convenes talks around November 6-8. The camps deadlock over on-the-spot questions versus the first debate's format, and Chiang's side cites schedule conflicts. The talks drag past November 13, or the debate quietly lapses.
- **Yes:** The media consortium meets this week. Under public pressure and with Chiang on record as "leaning toward" it, both sides agree on a date such as November 15-21. The date is announced around November 8-12.

(f) I start at about 30%. Chiang's explicit "lean toward participating" and the active media consortium push the forecast up. The incumbent's incentive to stall, the format friction and the short window pull it back down. On balance I move up to about 40%.

Probability: 40%

(a) There are about 10 days left, until 23:59 Taipei time on Nov 13, 2026. For Yes, a specific date for a second televised Chiang-Shen debate, other than the Oct 31 TVBS/SET event, must be publicly announced. The date has to be agreed by both campaigns, or confirmed by the host with both candidates participating.

(b) The status quo is No. As of Nov 3 no date exists, and the media consortium has not yet convened negotiations.

(c) Base rate: the Taipei mayoral races in 2018 and 2022 had a single televised debate despite pressure from challengers. The 2014 race had several. In races where the frontrunner resisted, a second debate got scheduled roughly 25-35% of the time. Once a frontrunner publicly says he is open, the rate is higher, though he can still slow the process down. Starting estimate: about 35%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Nov 3: Chiang said "我傾向於參加" (I lean toward taking part) and would join once format and time are agreed.
- Nov 2: The campaign managers, Wu and Lo, have made direct contact, and Lo says Chiang's side "has always been open."
- Oct 31: Ten outlets jointly issued an invitation.
- Oct 11-15: The first debate went from invitation to a fixed date in 4 days, so a date could come quickly once talks start.

Evidence for No:
- Chiang is the frontrunner (Kalshi 0.60) and a post-debate TVBS poll judged Shen the better performer, so Chiang has little incentive to hurry.
- Chiang's side keeps saying it is "waiting for the invitation," a classic stalling posture.
- The format is in dispute: Shen wants questions answered on the spot without advance sharing, and there is friction over the questions shared before the first debate.
- The host group is led by the DPP-leaning Liberty Times.
- From Nov 13 onward the official campaign period and CEC policy presentations fill the schedule.
- Chiang only "leans toward" taking part.

(e) No scenario: The consortium meets around Nov 6-8. Talks bog down over advance sharing of questions, cross-examination rules and dates. Chiang's camp cites a crowded campaign calendar, and Nov 13 passes with "still coordinating."

Yes scenario: The consortium convenes this week. Chiang, who has publicly committed to "leaning" toward a debate and is under media pressure, accepts a date around Nov 15-20. The organizers announce it by Nov 10.

(f) Chiang's public softening and the fast precedent from the first debate push me up from 35%. The frontrunner's incentives, the format disputes, the tight 10-day window and the stalling posture pull me back down. Net, I land near the base rate, slightly above it.

Probability: 38%

Once a second debate is publicly "leaned toward" and a media consortium is actively inviting, though, it often does get scheduled. A blended reference class gives roughly 35-45%.
